KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:14/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:14/r4.speaker: Eski tefsirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:14/r4.claim: Older commentaries describe the earth as initially flat and too unstable for habitation, then stabilized when God placed mountains upon it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:14/r4.anchor: Eski tefsirlerde “O (Allah), sizi sarsmaması için yere sağlam dağlar yerleştirdi” ifadesi açıklanırken, dünyanın önce dümdüz ve üzerinde ikamet edilemeyecek kadar hareketli olduğu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:14/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:14/r5.speaker: Muhammed Esed
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:14/r5.claim: Esed argues that the mountain-as-stake/support verses point to the earth’s crust hardening over magma and gas, largely preventing eruptions and making the earth habitable.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:14/r5.anchor: dağların birer kazık veya destek yapıldığını ifade eden âyette yer kabuğunun sertleşme sürecine değinildiği; yani yer kabuğunun, yer altındaki mağma ve gaz tabakalarının üzerini kapatıp dışa püskürmesini büyük ölçüde önleyecek bir yapı kazanmasıyla

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:14/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:14/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:14/r6.claim: The authors find Esed’s geological interpretation of the mountain verses reasonable.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:14/r6.anchor: Muhammed Esed’in ileri sürdüğü görüş (II, 531-532) bizce de mâkul görünmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:14/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:14/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:14/r7.claim: Mountainous ground is generally firm, so buildings there suffer less earthquake damage than buildings in valleys and plains, which are relatively risky.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:14/r7.anchor: Özellikle yeryüzünün dağlık kısımlarında zemin sağlam olduğu için, yapıların depremlerde daha az hasar görmesine karşılık vadilerin ve ovaların nisbeten riskli olduğu da bilinmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:14/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:14/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:14/r8.claim: Mountains also help maintain balance and order in terrestrial movements.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:14/r8.anchor: dağların yer hareketlerinde denge ve düzeni sağlama (balans) işlevinin bulunduğudur.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Classical Arabic leaves recoverable components unspoken in the constructions about paths and landmarks; the translation supplies the omitted wording.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Some components are suppressed here in accordance with a linguistic style of classical Arabic. They have been expressed in the translation.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: God placed mountains on earth to maintain its balance.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: God has planted mountains in the earth which maintain its balance.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: God made canals flow through the earth, benefiting human beings.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: He has made canals to flow in it which are beneficial for human beings.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: God made paths so people could travel between places.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: paths in the earth so that people can travel from one place to anofther.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: These created blessings imply that worship is due to God rather than deities that created none of them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: should He be worshipped or other deities who have not created any of these things?

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514/r4.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514/r4.claim: A report says the earth initially convulsed after its creation and angels feared it would not support anyone; by morning mountains anchored it, though the angels did not know what they were made from. It is also transmitted from Wahb ibn Munabbih.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514/r4.anchor: قيل: خلق الله الأرض فجعلت تمور فقالت الملائكة: ما هي بمقر أحد على ظهرها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514/r5.claim: “Rivers” is coordinated with “mountains”; alqā means “made,” supported by other Qurʾānic descriptions of making mountains and earth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514/r5.anchor: وعطف وأنهارا على رواسي. ومعنى ألقى: جعل، ألا ترى إلى قوله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514/r6.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyyah argues that alqā is more specific than “created” or “made”: God brought mountains into being by His power and invention, rather than from the earth itself.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: قال المتأولون: ألقى بمعنى خلق وجعل، وهي عندي أخص من خلق وجعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyyah supports his interpretation with the story of the unstable earth and says it is also narrated from Wahb ibn Munabbih.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514/r7.anchor: ويؤيد هذا النظر ما روي في القصص عن الحسن، عن قيس بن عباد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514/r8.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyyah parses “and rivers” with an implied verb, “He made” or “created”; he argues that the shared ellipsis proves alqā is more specific than “created.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514/r8.anchor: وقوله: وأنهارا، منصوب بفعل مضمر تقديره: وجعل، أو خلق أنهارا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514/r9.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects Ibn ʿAṭiyyah’s claim of consensus: interpreters explicitly report that alqā means “created” or “made.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514/r9.anchor: وأي إجماع في هذا، وقد حكي عن المتأولين أن ألقى بمعنى خلق وجعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514/r10.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī supplies an implied “He made rivers,” since alqā carries the sense of jaʿala, and cites the earth-as-bed verse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514/r10.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وأنهارا، وجعل فيها أنهارا لأن ألقى فيه معنى جعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514/r11.speaker: أبو البقاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514/r11.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ says the phrase may mean that God split rivers, and that “landmarks” means placing signs; the latter may coordinate with mountains.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514/r11.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: أي وشق أنهارا وعلامات أي: وضع علامات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514/r12.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514/r12.claim: Al-Rāzī notes that rational sciences establish that most rivers begin at mountain springs, explaining why rivers follow mountains in the sequence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514/r12.anchor: ثبت في العلوم العقلية أن أكثر الأنهار إنما تتفجر منابعها في الجبال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514/r13.claim: The roads lead to people’s destinations and allow them to find their way; another interpretation makes the guidance a lesson toward the Creator, truth, and God’s religion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p514/r13.anchor: وسبلا طرقا إلى مقاصدكم لعلكم تهتدون بالسبل إلى مقاصدكم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p13/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p13/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p13/r1.claim: The mountains keep the earth from moving; mayd means agitation and rocking, and sea-sickness is also called mayd.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p13/r1.anchor: أي تتحرك وتميل. والميد: هو الاضطراب والتكفؤ، ومنه قيل للدوار الذي يعتري راكب البحر: ميد.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p13/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p13/r2.speaker: وهب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p13/r2.claim: Wahb reports that the newly created earth swayed until mountains were set on it; the angels had not known what mountains were created from.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p13/r2.anchor: قال وهب: لما خلق الله الأرض جعلت تمور فقالت الملائكة: إن هذه غير مقرة أحدا على ظهرها فأصبحت وقد أرسيت بالجبال

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p13/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p13/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p13/r3.claim: God made rivers and varied roads so people can reach their destinations without getting lost.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p13/r3.anchor: وجعل فيها أنهارا وطرقا مختلفة، {لعلكم تهتدون} إلى ما تريدون فلا تضلون.

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:15-16/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:15-16/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:15-16/r1.claim: Mountains were placed on earth to prevent it from leaning or shaking; the earth's original light, simple nature should have made it rotate like the spheres or move from slight causes, while the mountains' weight toward the center anchors it like pegs.
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:15-16/r1.anchor: وكان من حقها أن تتحرك بالاستدارة كالأفلاك، أو أن تتحرك بأدنى سبب للتحريك

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:15-16/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:15-16/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:15-16/r2.claim: Another account says the earth shook when created, the angels feared it could not support anyone, and it was then fixed by mountains.
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:15-16/r2.anchor: وقيل لما خلق الله الأرض جعلت تمور فقالت الملائكة: ما هي بمقر أحد

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:15-16/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:15-16/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:15-16/r3.claim: Rivers were made in the earth because the verb for casting also governs them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:15-16/r3.anchor: وجعل فيها أنهارا لأن ألقى فيه معناه

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:15-16/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:15-16/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:15-16/r4.claim: Paths help people reach their destinations or lead them to knowledge of God.
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:15-16/r4.anchor: لمقاصدكم، أو إلى معرفة الله سبحانه وتعالى

BIQAI-FULL:v4p254/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p254/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p254/r1.claim: God placed firm mountains on earth like pegs, touching and ornamenting its regions, to prevent it from swaying and causing people motion sickness.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p254/r1.anchor: جبالا { رواسي } مماسة لها ومزينة لنواحيها , كراهة { أن تميد } أي تميل مضطربة يمينا وشمالا

BIQAI-FULL:v4p254/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p254/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p254/r2.claim: The earth's stability is shown by the surrounding mention of seas and rivers: even slight daily movement would flood the seas down the slope and reverse river channels, turning their benefits into harms.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p254/r2.anchor: وأدل دليل على ثبات الأرض ما سبقها من ذكر البحار , ولحقها من الحديث عن الأنهار , فإنها لو تحركت ولو بمقدار شعرة في كل يوم

BIQAI-FULL:v4p254/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p254/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p254/r3.claim: If the rivers' inflow accumulated in the seas over time, the seas would overflow and inundate the earth.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p254/r3.anchor: ولو زادت البحار , بما تصب فيها الأنهار , على مر الليل وكر النهار , لأغرقت الأرض

BIQAI-FULL:v4p254/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p254/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p254/r4.claim: The author describes a yearly water cycle: summer and seasonal solar heat penetrates the earth and remains in its depths through winter, warming seas and other waters.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p254/r4.anchor: بأن سلط حرارة الشمس على الأرض في جميع مدة الصيف وبعض غيره من الفصول , فسرت في أغوارها , وحميت في أعماقها في الشتاء

BIQAI-FULL:v4p254/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p254/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p254/r5.claim: Warmed waters evaporate in an amount corresponding to river inflow, like vapor rising from a boiling pot.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p254/r5.anchor: فأسخنت مياه البحار وغيرها فتصاعدت منها بخارات كما يتصاعد من القدر المغلي

BIQAI-FULL:v4p254/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p254/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p254/r6.claim: The vapor cools and condenses into rain, which revives the earth and replenishes rivers; annual recurrence keeps sea levels from increasing.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p254/r6.anchor: فانعقدت تلك البخارات في الجو مياها لما بردت , فنزل منها المطر , فأحيا الأرض بعد موتها , وتخلل أعماقها منه ما شاء الله , فأمد الأنهار

BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r1.claim: Mountains, seas, and rivers provide access to the benefits of each, and they serve as signs for physical and spiritual routes.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r1.anchor: ولما ذكر ذلك , أتبعه ما يتوصل به إلى منافع كل منه

BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r2.claim: The routes help people reach their destinations.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p255/r2.anchor: أي يحصل الاهتداء فتهتدوا إلى مقاصدكم

DURR-FULL:v5p118/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p118/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v5p118/r1.claim: An unattributed exchange says water is stronger than fire, wind stronger than water, man stronger than wind, and woman stronger than man.
DURR-FULL:v5p118/r1.anchor: هل من خلقك شيء أشد من النار قال: نعم الماء قالوا: ربنا هل من خلقك شيء هو أشد من الماء

DURR-FULL:v5p118/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p118/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p118/r2.claim: Rawasi are mountains that fix the earth so that it does not sway; without them, creatures could not remain settled.
DURR-FULL:v5p118/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {رواسي} قال: الجبال {أن تميد بكم} قال: أثبتها بالجبال

DURR-FULL:v5p118/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p118/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p118/r3.claim: Before God set the mountains as stakes, the earth moved and would not settle.
DURR-FULL:v5p118/r3.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {رواسي أن تميد بكم} قال: حتى لا تميد بكم كانوا على الأرض تمور بهم لا يستقر بها

DURR-FULL:v5p118/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p118/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p118/r4.claim: The earth's swaying means it might overturn with its inhabitants; rivers are found in every town.
DURR-FULL:v5p118/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله: {إن تميد بكم} قال: أن تكفأ بكم

DURR-FULL:v5p118/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p118/r5.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p118/r5.anchor: وفي قوله: وأنهارا قال: بكل بلدة

DURR-FULL:v5p118/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p118/r6.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v5p118/r6.claim: The paths are routes between the mountains.
DURR-FULL:v5p118/r6.anchor: عن السدي في قوله: {وسبلا} قال: السبل هي الطرق بين الجبال

DURR-FULL:v5p118/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p118/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p118/r7.claim: The paths are roads and the signs are stars.
DURR-FULL:v5p118/r7.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {وسبلا} قال: طرقا {وعلامات} قال: هي النجوم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p120#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p120#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p120#2/r1.claim: The passage shifts to evidence and gratitude for great creatures on Earth’s surface that benefit people; calling their creation ‘casting’ pictures them as additions placed on a completed Earth, perhaps created later.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p120#2/r1.anchor: انتقال إلى الاستدلال والامتنان بما على سطح الأرض من المخلوقات العظيمة التي في وجودها لطف بالإنسان . وهذه المخلوقات لما كانت مجعولة كالتكملة للأرض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p120#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p120#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p120#2/r2.claim: Ibn Ashur suggests mountains may have emerged through great seismic disturbances and rivers through heavy rain; roads and markers clearly came later, making all four resemble objects cast onto something complete.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p120#2/r2.anchor: ولعل خلقها كان متأخرا عن خلق الأرض ، إذ لعل الجبال انبثقت باضطرابات أرضية كالزلزال العظيم ثم حدثت الأنهار بتهاطل الأمطار .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p120#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p120#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p120#2/r3.claim: He also proposes that mountains formed from debris cast off by celestial bodies and rain formed rivers; ‘casting’ fits these naturally and extends to routes and markers by generalization, as in 54:25 for giving revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p120#2/r3.anchor: ولعل أصل تكوين الجبال كان من شظايا رمت بها الكواكب فصادفت سطح الأرض ، كما أن الأمطار تهاطلت فكونت الأنهار ؛ فيكون تشبيه حصول هذين بالإلقاء بينا .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p120#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p120#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p120#2/r4.claim: Rawāsi is a plural of rās from rusu, firmness and settling; it has variant pronunciations, is used as a conventional name for a mountain, and its fawāʿil plural is irregular like ʿawādhil and fawāris, with earlier discussion at 13:3.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p120#2/r4.anchor: ورواسي } جمع راس . وهو وصف من الرسو بفتح الراء وسكون السين . ويقال بضم الراء والسين مشددة وتشديد الواو . وهو الثبات والتمكن في المكان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p121/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p121/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p121/r1.claim: Ibn Ashur reads the poetic example as a causal phrase whose intended result is avoiding a curse, not bringing one about.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p121/r1.anchor: أراد أن لا تشتمونا . فالعلة هي انتفاء الشتم لا وقوعه .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p121/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p121/r2.speaker: عمرو بن كلثوم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p121/r2.claim: Amr ibn Kulthum’s line ‘we hastened hospitality lest you curse us’ illustrates the implied negation: the intended cause is preventing the curse, not bringing it about.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p121/r2.anchor: فعجلنا القرى أن تشتمونا أراد أن لا تشتمونا . فالعلة هي انتفاء الشتم لا وقوعه .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p121/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p121/r3.speaker: نحاة الكوفة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p121/r3.claim: Kufan grammarians explain this construction by deleting the negative particle after an: ‘so that Earth would not shake beneath you.’ Ibn Ashur calls this the apparent analysis.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p121/r3.anchor: ونحاة الكوفة يخرجون أمثال ذلك على حذف حرف النفي بعد { أن } . والتقدير : لأن لا تميد بكم ولئلا تشتمونا ، وهو الظاهر .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p121/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p121/r4.speaker: نحاة البصرة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p121/r4.claim: Basran grammarians instead posit an omitted verbal noun between the causal verb and an: ‘for fear that Earth would shake beneath you.’
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p121/r4.anchor: ونحاة البصرة يخرجون مثله على حذف مضاف بين الفعل المعلل و { أن } . تقديره : كراهية أن تميد بكم .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p121/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p121/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p121/r5.claim: The verse points to a subtle mechanism: mountains’ elevations may balance Earth’s roundness so it is not so smooth that its motion through space causes severe disturbance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p121/r5.anchor: ولعل الله جعل نتوء الجبال على سطح الأرض معدلا لكرويتها بحيث لا تكون بحد من الملاسة يخفف حركتها في الفضاء تخفيفا يوجب شدة اضطرابها .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p121/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p121/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p121/r6.claim: Rivers are a great blessing because people drink from them, irrigate fields with them, and use them for boat travel.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p121/r6.anchor: ونعمة الأنهار عظيمة ، فإن منها شرابهم وسقي حرثهم ، وفيها تجري سفنهم لأسفارهم .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p121/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p121/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p121/r7.claim: ‘Paths’ is attached to the prior mention of rivers because their travel benefit is the latest blessing named; sabīl here means an overland route.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p121/r7.anchor: ولهذه المنة الأخيرة عطف عليها { وسبلا } جمع سبيل . وهو الطريق الذي يسافر فيه برا .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p121/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p121/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p121/r8.claim: The parenthetical ‘so that you may be guided’ concerns both practical travel, using routes, river moorings, and distances, and guidance to monotheism through signs of the sole Creator; these provisions arise through God’s inspiration.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p121/r8.anchor: وجملة { لعلكم تهتدون } معترضة ، أي رجاء اهتدائكم . وهو كلام موجه يصلح للاهتداء إلى المقاصد في الأسفار من رسم الطرق وإقامة المراسي على الأنهار واعتبار المسافات .

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p563/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p563/r1.speaker: الحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p563/r1.claim: Al-Hasan says the newly created earth shook so much that people feared no one could live on it; by morning mountains had been created, whose origin the angels did not know.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p563/r1.anchor: سمعت الحسن يقول: لما خلقت الأرض كانت تميد، فقالوا ما هذه بمقرة على ظهرها أحدا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p563/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p563/r2.speaker: قيس بن عبادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p563/r2.claim: Qays ibn ʿUbada reports that the earth heaved when created, prompting the angels' concern, and by morning its stabilizing mountains were in place.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p563/r2.anchor: عن قيس بن عبادة: أن الله تعالى لما خلق الأرض، جعلت تمور، فقالت الملائكة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p563/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p563/r3.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p563/r3.claim: Ali says the earth trembled and complained that people would commit sins and impurity upon it; God anchored it with visible and unseen mountains, yet it still quivered like trembling flesh.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p563/r3.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب (7) ، رضي الله عنه، قال: لما خلق الله الأرض قمصت وقالت: أي رب

JISHUMI:v6p4010/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4010/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4010/r1.claim: The verses point to God's great blessings in the animals, trees, fruits, and other things He created and subjected for people's benefit.
JISHUMI:v6p4010/r1.anchor: تدل الآية على عظيم نعمه تعالى بما خلق وسخر من أنواع الحيوان والأشجار والثمار وغير ذلك. وتدل على أنه خلق جميع ذلك لمنافع خلقه

JISHUMI:v6p4010/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4010/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4010/r2.claim: God intends people to reflect on creation; this makes reasoning obligatory and undermines uncritical imitation. Reflection is an act of people, so commands and encouragement to reflect are sound.
JISHUMI:v6p4010/r2.anchor: وتدل على أنه أراد من خلقه التفكر فيه فيوجب النظر ويفسد التقليد. وتدل على أن النظر والتفكر فعل العبد ليصح الأمر به، والبعث عليه

JISHUMI:v6p4010/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4010/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4010/r5.claim: Mayd is movement or swaying from side to side; the word for a dining table is also connected with feeding or dining.
JISHUMI:v6p4010/r5.anchor: والميد: الاضطراب، ماد يميد ميدا إذا تحركت ومالت يمينا ويسارا، ومادت الغصن تمايلت. والمائدة معروفة

JISHUMI:v6p4010/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4010/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4010/r6.claim: Some derive māʾida from mada, “to feed,” while others connect it to the expression “he dined me.”
JISHUMI:v6p4010/r6.anchor: قيل: هي من ماد تميد إذا أطعم. وقيل: مادني يميدني إذا تعشى، والمائدة منه

JISHUMI:v6p4010/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4010/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4010/r8.claim: “Rivers and paths” is accusative with an omitted verb understood as “He made rivers and paths.”
JISHUMI:v6p4010/r8.anchor: قيل: نصب (وأنهارا وسبلا) بمحذوف، وتقديره: جعل أنهارا وسبلا

MUQATIL:16:14-17/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:16:14-17/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:16:14-17/r2.claim: God set mountains in the earth to keep it from moving and swaying its inhabitants, and provided flowing rivers and roads so people can find their way.
MUQATIL:16:14-17/r2.anchor: يعني الجبال، { أن تميد بكم } ، يعني لئلا تزول بكم الأرض فتميل بمن عليها

RAZI-FULL:v20p7#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p7#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p7#2/r1.claim: This passage begins by naming some of God's blessings created on earth.
RAZI-FULL:v20p7#2/r1.anchor: المقصود من هذه الآية ذكر بعض النعم التي خلقها الله تعالى في الأرض

RAZI-FULL:v20p7#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p7#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p7#2/r2.claim: For an tamīda bikum, Kufans understand “so it does not shake,” while Basrans understand “out of dislike that it shake”; mayd is movement and swaying right and left, discussed at 4:176.
RAZI-FULL:v20p7#2/r2.anchor: قوله : { أن تميد بكم } يعني لئلا تميد بكم على قول الكوفيين وكراهة أن تميد بكم على قول البصريين

RAZI-FULL:v20p7#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p7#2/r3.speaker: الجمهور
RAZI-FULL:v20p7#2/r3.claim: The majority compare the earth on water to a boat: it wavered until God set heavy mountains on it like anchors, making it stable.
RAZI-FULL:v20p7#2/r3.anchor: المشهور عن الجمهور في تفسير هذه الآية أن قالوا : إن السفينة إذا ألقيت على وجه الماء ، فإنها تميد من جانب إلى جانب

RAZI-FULL:v20p7#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p7#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p7#2/r4.claim: Rāzī objects that if earth is naturally heavier than water it would sink rather than float and wobble like a hollow wooden boat; if natures do not cause motion, God's creation of movement and rest makes the mountain explanation fail.
RAZI-FULL:v20p7#2/r4.anchor: هذا التعليل مشكل على كل التقديرات

RAZI-FULL:v20p8/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p8/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p8/r1.claim: A further objection asks what keeps the supporting water in its place: if its nature does so, the same account could explain the earth; if God does, He could directly keep the earth still.
RAZI-FULL:v20p8/r1.anchor: فما المقتضى لسكون ذلك الماء ووقوفه في حيزه المخصوص

RAZI-FULL:v20p8/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p8/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p8/r2.claim: A third objection is that movement of the entire enormous earth over the sea would be imperceptible; proponents compare it to a passenger not sensing a moving ship, while Rāzī replies that visible quakes move only a small part.
RAZI-FULL:v20p8/r2.anchor: أن مجموع الأرض جسم عظيم ، فبتقدير أن تميد كليته وتضطرب على وجه البحر المحيط لم تظهر تلك الحالة للناس

RAZI-FULL:v20p8/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p8/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p8/r3.claim: Rāzī's own approach begins from the demonstrable spherical shape of earth and treats its mountains as surface roughnesses.
RAZI-FULL:v20p8/r3.anchor: ثبت بالدلائل اليقينية أن الأرض كرة ، وثبت أن هذه الجبال على سطح هذه الكرة جارية مجرى خشونات

RAZI-FULL:v20p9/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p9/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p9/r1.claim: A smooth sphere would rotate with little cause, while massive mountains directed toward the world's center act like pegs that prevent earth's rotation, wobbling, and movement.
RAZI-FULL:v20p9/r1.anchor: فكان تخليق هذه الجبال على وجه الأرض كالأوتاد المغروزة في الكرة المانعة لها عن الحركة المستديرة

RAZI-FULL:v20p9/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p9/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p9/r2.claim: “Rivers” is coordinated with mountains; although alqāʾ suggests casting downward, here it means making or creating, as shown by 50:7, 41:10, and “I cast love upon you” at 20:39.
RAZI-FULL:v20p9/r2.anchor: ألقى ا في الأرض أنهارا كما قال : { وألقينا فيها رواسي }

RAZI-FULL:v20p9/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p9/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p9/r3.claim: The expression of casting can approximate bringing down from above, but in these examples it means creation or making rather than literal throwing.
RAZI-FULL:v20p9/r3.anchor: إلا أن المراد من هذا الإلقاء الجعل والخلق قال تعالى : { وألقيت عليك محبة منى }

RAZI-FULL:v20p9#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p9#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p9#2/r1.claim: Rational sciences establish that most rivers rise from springs in mountains, explaining why rivers follow mountains in the verse.
RAZI-FULL:v20p9#2/r1.anchor: ثبت في العلوم العقلية أن أكثر الأنهار إنما تتفجر منابعها في الجبال

RAZI-FULL:v20p9#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p9#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p9#2/r2.claim: Paths are also coordinated with mountains: God laid them out so travelers could find their way, as in 20:53; “so that you may be guided” states their purpose.
RAZI-FULL:v20p9#2/r2.anchor: وهي أيضا على قوله : { وألقى فى الارض رواسى } والتقدير : وألقى في الأرض سبلا ومعناه : أنه تعالى أظهرها وبينها

TABATABAI:16:14-16/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:14-16/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:14-16/r2.claim: The term may mean that mountains were placed on earth so it would not sway or tilt from side to side and disrupt human livelihood.
TABATABAI:16:14-16/r2.anchor: الميد الميل يمينا وشمالا وهو الاضطراب ماد يميد ميدا. انتهى. وقوله { أن تميد بكم } أي كراهة أن تميد بكم

TABATABAI:16:14-16/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:14-16/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:14-16/r3.claim: God made rivers flow and carry water to fields and gardens, people, and domestic animals.
TABATABAI:16:14-16/r3.anchor: وجعل فيها أنهارا تجري بمائها وتسوقه إلى مزارعكم وبساتينكم وتسقيكم وما عندكم من الحيوان الأهلي.

TABATABAI:16:14-16/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:14-16/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:14-16/r4.claim: Paths include natural open passages between places and constructed tracks made by human travel or labor; the context encompasses both.
TABATABAI:16:14-16/r4.anchor: والسبل منها ما هي طبيعية وهي المسافات الواقعة بين بقعتين من الأرض الواصلة إحداهما بالأخرى من غير أن يقطع ما بينهما بحاجب أو مانع

TABATABAI:16:14-16/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:14-16/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:14-16/r5.claim: God may be credited with paths made by people because they arise from created things and their effects, just as human-made rivers or markers are included in divine making.
TABATABAI:16:14-16/r5.anchor: ولا ضير في نسبة ما جعله الإنسان إلى جعله تعالى كما نسب الأنهار والعلامات إلى جعله تعالى

TABRISI:16:15-16/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:15-16/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:15-16/r2.claim: Makhr is the splitting of water to either side; a ship is described as cutting through the water and is called mākhirah.
TABRISI:16:15-16/r2.anchor: المخر شق الماء من عن يمين وشمال مخرت السفينة

TABRISI:16:15-16/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:15-16/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:15-16/r3.claim: Makhr can also mean the sound of wind blowing forcefully.
TABRISI:16:15-16/r3.anchor: والمخر أيضا صوت هبوب الريح إذا اشتد هبوبها

TABRISI:16:15-16/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:15-16/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:15-16/r4.claim: To makhr the earth is to furrow it for cultivation.

TABRISI:16:15-16/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:15-16/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:15-16/r5.claim: To makhr land with water is to send water over it to improve it.
TABRISI:16:15-16/r5.anchor: ومخرها بالماء إذا أرسل عليها الماء لتطيب

TABRISI:16:15-16/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:15-16/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:15-16/r6.claim: Mayd means tilting or swaying from side to side, a movement expressed by māda yamīdu.
TABRISI:16:15-16/r6.anchor: والميد الميل يمينا وشمالا وهو الاضطراب

TABRISI:16:15-16/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:15-16/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:15-16/r8.claim: An tamīda bikum is purposive, with an implied sense of lest or for fear that the earth sway with you.
TABRISI:16:15-16/r8.anchor: في موضع نصب بأنه مفعول له وتقديره كراهة أن تميد بكم

TABRISI:16:15-16/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:15-16/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:15-16/r9.claim: Anhāran wa-subulan depends on an omitted jaʿala, since it cannot coordinate directly with alqā; two anonymous poetic examples illustrate such ellipsis.
TABRISI:16:15-16/r9.anchor: بمحذوف تقديره وجعل لكم أنهارا لدلالة

TABRISI:16:15-16/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:15-16/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:15-16/r12.claim: God subdued the sea, making it easy for people to travel over it and obtain its benefits.
TABRISI:16:15-16/r12.anchor: أي ذلله لكم وسهل لكم الطريق إلى ركوبه

TABRISI:16:15-16/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:15-16/r19.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:15-16/r19.claim: God placed firmly rooted mountains in the earth so it would not tilt or sway with people.
TABRISI:16:15-16/r19.anchor: أي جبالا عالية ثابتة واحدها راسية

TABRISI:16:15-16/r20.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:15-16/r20.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:15-16/r20.claim: The rivers and roads let people direct water to gardens and travel to the places they choose.
TABRISI:16:15-16/r20.anchor: أي طرقا لكي تجروا الماء في الأنهار

TABRISI:16:15-16/r21.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:15-16/r21.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:16:15-16/r21.claim: Some identify the rivers as the Nile, Euphrates, Tigris, Sayḥān, Jayḥān, and similar rivers.
TABRISI:16:15-16/r21.anchor: وقيل أراد بالأنهار النيل والفرات ودجلة

TABRISI:16:15-16/r22.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:15-16/r22.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:16:15-16/r22.claim: Another explanation takes guidance through the rivers and roads as guidance to God's oneness.
TABRISI:16:15-16/r22.anchor: وقيل لتهتدوا بها إلى توحيد الله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:13-16/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:13-16/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:13-16/r4.claim: God placed stable mountains so the earth would not shake, and made rivers such as the Nile, Euphrates, and Tigris, plus roads to towns so people can find their destinations.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:13-16/r4.anchor: جبالا ثابتة { أن تميد } لئلا تميد

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p55#2/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p55#2/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p55#2/r1.claim: The paths are routes by which people may find their way.

STUDYQURAN:16:15/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:15/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:15/r1.claim: A nearly identical verse appears at 21:31.
STUDYQURAN:16:15/r1.anchor: A nearly identical verse is 21:31; see 21:30–31c. God’s casting or placing firm mountains

STUDYQURAN:16:15/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:15/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:15/r2.claim: The mountains stabilize the earth so it does not shake beneath humanity.
STUDYQURAN:16:15/r2.anchor: God’s casting or placing firm mountains into the earth for humanity suggests their functioning as a source of stability for the earth, lest it shake beneath them

STUDYQURAN:16:15/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:15/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:15/r3.claim: Elsewhere mountains are described as stakes that hold up a tent.
STUDYQURAN:16:15/r3.anchor: where the mountains are described as stakes like those that hold up a tent.

STUDYQURAN:16:15/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:15/r4.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:16:15/r4.claim: Al-Rāzī suggests mountains and streams are paired because most streams originate in mountain springs.
STUDYQURAN:16:15/r4.anchor: Al-Rāzī suggests that mountains and streams are mentioned together (cf. 13:3; 27:61), because most streams have their origin in mountain springs.

STUDYQURAN:16:15/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:15/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:15/r5.claim: The stability of mountains will be overturned on the Last Day, when earth and mountains shake and mountains become shifting sand heaps.
STUDYQURAN:16:15/r5.anchor: The stability provided by the mountains will be overturned on the Last Day, however, which is described as a day on which the earth and the mountains shake

TAB-FULL:v14p190/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p190/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p190/r1.claim: Rawāsī is the plural of rāsiyah and means the firm mountains fixed in the earth.
TAB-FULL:v14p190/r1.anchor: وألقى في الأرض رواسي أن تميد بكم

TAB-FULL:v14p190/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p190/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p190/r2.claim: The clause means “lest the earth sway with you,” with “not” understood, as in 4:176 where God makes matters clear so that people do not go astray.
TAB-FULL:v14p190/r2.anchor: وألقى في الأرض رواسي أن تميد بكم

TAB-FULL:v14p190/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p190/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p190/r3.claim: God anchored the earth with mountains to stop its inhabitants from being shaken; it had been moving before the mountains were set in place.
TAB-FULL:v14p190/r3.anchor: أرسى الأرض بالجبال لئلا يميد خلقه الذي على ظهرها، بل وقد كانت مائدة قبل أن ترسى بها

TAB-FULL:v14p190/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p190/r4.speaker: قيس بن عباد
TAB-FULL:v14p190/r4.claim: A report from Qays ibn ʿAbbād says the newly created earth churned and the angels feared it could not bear anyone; by morning its mountains had appeared.
TAB-FULL:v14p190/r4.anchor: عن قيس بن عباد: " أن الله تبارك وتعالى لما خلق الأرض جعلت تمور

TAB-FULL:v14p190/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p190/r5.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
TAB-FULL:v14p190/r5.claim: ʿAlī reports that the earth heaved and protested that people would sin and make it foul; God anchored it with visible and unseen mountains, leaving it stable like quivering flesh.
TAB-FULL:v14p190/r5.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب، قال: " لما خلق الله الأرض قمصت

TAB-FULL:v14p190/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p190/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p190/r6.claim: Mayd means unsteady movement or rocking; a ship may roll and tilt with its passengers, and the word also names sea sickness or vertigo.
TAB-FULL:v14p190/r6.anchor: والميد: هو الاضطراب والتكفؤ، يقال: مادت السفينة تميد ميدا: إذا تكفأت بأهلها ومالت

TAB-FULL:v14p190/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p190/r7.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v14p190/r7.claim: Mujahid glosses the clause as meaning that the earth might tilt with you.
TAB-FULL:v14p190/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد: " {أن تميد بكم} [النحل: 15] أن تكفأ بكم

TAB-FULL:v14p190/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p190/r8.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v14p190/r8.claim: Al-Hasan says the mountains keep the earth from swaying; he also says it nearly moved at creation, then mountains appeared, whose origin the angels did not know.
TAB-FULL:v14p190/r8.anchor: عن قتادة، عن الحسن، في قوله: {وألقى في الأرض رواسي أن تميد بكم} [النحل: 15]

TAB-FULL:v14p191/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p191/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p191/r1.claim: “And rivers” is coordinated with the mountains and shares the implied verb “He placed/made”; the intended meaning is clear despite the verb not being repeated, as in the cited rajaz line where a non-heard quality is coordinated with sound.
TAB-FULL:v14p191/r1.anchor: فعطف بالأنهار على الرواسي، وأعمل فيها ما أعمل في الرواسي، إذ كان مفهوما معنى الكلام والمراد منه

TAB-FULL:v14p191#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p191#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p191#2/r1.claim: Subul is the plural of sabīl, like ṭuruq is the plural of ṭarīq; the paths and passes let people travel for their needs and livelihoods, as a mercy and blessing.

TAB-FULL:v14p191#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p191#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v14p191#2/r2.claim: Qatada glosses subul as roads or routes, citing the same word in 20:53.

TAB-FULL:v14p191#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p191#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p191#2/r3.claim: The paths allow people to find their intended places and destinations without getting lost or confused.
TAB-FULL:v14p191#2/r3.anchor: لكي تهتدوا بهذه السبل التي جعلها لكم في الأرض إلى الأماكن التي تقصدون، والمواضع التي تريدون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p34/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p34/r2.speaker: الكوفيون والبصريون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p34/r2.claim: The Kufans parse the clause as “lest it sway with you”; the Basrans understand it as “in dislike of its swaying with you.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p34/r2.anchor: يعني لئلا تميد على قول الكوفيين، وكراهة أن تميد على قول البصريين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p34/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p34/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p34/r3.claim: Mayd means movement and disturbance from side to side.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p34/r3.anchor: والميد: الحركة والاضطراب يمينا وشمالا، ماد يميد ميدا (¬1)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p34/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p34/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p34/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says God pegged the earth down with mountains so it would not sway with its inhabitants.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p34/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد أوتدها بالجبال لئلا تميد بأهلها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p34/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p34/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p34/r5.claim: The rivers intended include the Nile, Euphrates, Tigris, Sayhan, and Jayhan.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p34/r5.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {وأنهارا} قال يريد: النيل (¬2) والفرات ودجلة (¬3) وسيحان (¬4) وجيحان (¬5)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p34/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p34/r6.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p34/r6.claim: “And rivers” is accusative with an understood “and He made”; the prior “cast” conveys the sense of making, as shown by “the mountains as pegs” at 78:7.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p34/r6.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: لأن معنى {وألقى في الأرض رواسي}: جعل فيها رواسي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p34/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p34/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p34/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says the paths are routes to every land, so that people can find their destinations without getting lost.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p34/r7.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {وسبلا} قال ابن عباس: يريد طرقا إلى كل بلاد (¬2)، {ولعلكم تهتدون}: لكي تهتدوا إلى مقاصدكم

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p55/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p55/r7.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p55/r7.claim: The firmly set رواسي are mountains.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p55/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p55/r8.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p55/r8.claim: The mountains keep the earth from shaking beneath you.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p55/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p55/r9.speaker: عاصم بن حكيم وابن مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p55/r9.claim: A report from Abū Mujāhid glosses the phrase as the earth not tipping you over.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p55/r9.anchor: عاصم بن حكيم وابن مجاهد، عن أبيه، قال: أن تكفأ بكم.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p55/r10.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p55/r10.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p55/r10.claim: God also made rivers in the earth.

BURHAN:v4p393/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p393/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p393/r3.claim: La'alla can mean in order that; Tha'lab also takes the phrase about Moses speaking gently so Pharaoh may remember causally.
BURHAN:v4p393/r3.anchor: الثاني للتعليل كقوله تعالى ﴿ فاتبعوه واتقوا لعلكم ترحمون ﴾

BURHAN:v4p393/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p393/r8.speaker: الرمانى
BURHAN:v4p393/r8.claim: Al-Rummani says a past-tense clause cannot serve as the predicate after la'alla.
BURHAN:v4p393/r8.anchor: وممن نص على منع وقوع الماضي خبرا للعل الرماني

ITQAN:v3p170/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p170/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p170/r4.claim: The negative particle لا is regularly omitted from a negated imperfect in an oath response and is also understood in other examples, including so that the earth not sway.
ITQAN:v3p170/r4.anchor: حذف ( لا ) النافية يطرد في جواب القسم إذا كان المنفي مضارعا نحو ﴿ تالله تفتأ ﴾ وورد في غيره نحو ﴿ وعلى الذين يطيقونه فدية ﴾ أي لا يطيقونه

DAMGHANI:v1p418/r7.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p418/r7.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p418/r7.claim: Alqā can mean to create, as in God's creating mountains on earth; the source also cites Qāf.
DAMGHANI:v1p418/r7.anchor: ألقى أي خلق قوله تعالى في سورة النحل

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p242#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p242#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p242#4/r1.claim: Rawāsī are firmly fixed mountains that do not move; anything fixed is said to have settled (rasā).
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p242#4/r1.anchor: {وألقى في الأرض رواسي} أي: جبالا ثوابت لا تبرح. وكل شيء ثبت فقد رسا.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p242#4/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p242#4/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p242#4/r2.claim: The phrase means lest the earth move beneath you; mayd is movement or inclination.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p242#4/r2.anchor: {أن تميد بكم} أي: لئلا تميد بكم الأرض. والميد: الحركة والميل.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p242#4/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p242#4/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p242#4/r3.claim: A person who yamīd in his walk sways from side to side.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p242#4/r3.anchor: ومنه يقال: فلان يميد في مشيته: إذا تكفأ (2) .

MAJAZ:v1p357/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p357/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p357/r2.claim: Rawāsi are firmly established mountains that God placed in the earth.
MAJAZ:v1p357/r2.anchor: «وألقى في الأرض رواسي» (15) أي جعل فيها جبالا ثوابت قد رست

MAJAZ:v1p357/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p357/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p357/r3.claim: An tamīda bikum means so that the earth does not sway or tilt with you.
MAJAZ:v1p357/r3.anchor: «أن تميد بكم» (15) مجازه: أن لا تميل بكم. «أيان يبعثون» (21) مجازه

SAMIN-DURR:16:15/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:15/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:15/r1.claim: أن تميد means 'lest it sway' or 'to prevent it from swaying.'
SAMIN-DURR:16:15/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { أن تميد }:، أي: كراهة أن تميد، أو: لئلا تميد.

SAMIN-DURR:16:15/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:15/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:15/r2.claim: وأنهارا coordinates with رواسي because إلقاء here means creating; the author rejects Ibn ʿAtiyya's analysis with an elided verb.
SAMIN-DURR:16:15/r2.anchor: قوله: " وأنهارا " عطف على " رواسي " لأن الإلقاء بمعنى الخلق. وادعاء ابن عطية أنه منصوب بفعل مضمر، أي: وجعل فيها أنهارا، ليس كما ذكره.

SAMIN-DURR:16:15/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:15/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:16:15/r3.claim: Abu al-Baqa supplies an omitted verb meaning 'and he cut rivers through it,' which the author calls apt.
SAMIN-DURR:16:15/r3.anchor: وقدره أبو البقاء: " وشق فيها أنهارا " وهو مناسب،

SAMIN-DURR:16:15/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:15/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:15/r4.claim: سبلا can be understood with an implicit 'made them passable' or 'placed roads in it.'
SAMIN-DURR:16:15/r4.anchor: و " سبلا " ، أي: وذلل، أو: وجعل فيها طرقا.

ZAJJAJ:v3p193/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p193/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p193/r2.claim: Rawāsi are fixed, firmly grounded mountains.

ZAJJAJ:v3p193/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p193/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p193/r3.claim: The phrase means lest the earth sway or fail to remain stable.

ZAJJAJ:v3p193/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p193/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p193/r4.claim: Māda al-rajul yamīdu can mean to become dizzy; al-maydā refers to people who become dizzy while riding at sea.
ZAJJAJ:v3p193/r4.anchor: يقال ماد الرجل يميد ميدا، إذا دير به

ZAJJAJ:v3p193/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p193/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p193/r5.claim: The clause an tamīda is accusative as an object expressing cause.
ZAJJAJ:v3p193/r5.anchor: (أن تميد) في موضع نصب، مفعول لها

ZAJJAJ:v3p193/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p193/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p193/r6.claim: The sense supplies a verb: God placed mountains, rivers, and roads in the earth; alqā here means jaʿala.
ZAJJAJ:v3p193/r6.anchor: المعنى وجعل فيها رواسي وأنهارا وسبلا

ZAJJAJ:v3p193/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p193/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p193/r7.claim: The explanation that God placed mountains in the earth is supported by the description of mountains as pegs.

ASAD-NOTES:16:15#n11/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:16:15#n11/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:16:15#n11/r1.claim: Asad explains mountain uplift as part of the crust's gradual balancing during cooling and hardening; pressure from overlying material, especially mountains, supports a partly solid interior.
ASAD-NOTES:16:15#n11/r1.anchor: the mountains owe their rise to the gradual balancing process to which the solid crust of the earth is subject

ASAD-NOTES:16:15#n11/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:16:15#n11/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:16:15#n11/r2.claim: Asad says this relative, quake-and-volcano-disrupted equilibrium makes life possible; “lest it sway with you” refers to the solid crust against an unstable interior, with mountains as the “pegs” of 78:7.
ASAD-NOTES:16:15#n11/r2.anchor: it is the solidity of the earth's crust - as contrasted with its possibly fluid but certainly very unstable interior - which makes life on earth possible

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8/r1.claim: Quranic verse endings are often musically harmonious; this has a marked effect on hearing and on the soul.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8/r1.anchor: يعنى بهذا الانسجام عناية واضحة لما لذلك من تأثير كبير على السمع ووقع مؤثر في النفس

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8/r5.claim: Similar blessings-counting verses end differently, with كفار in Ibrahim and رحيم in al-Nahl, matching each sura's surrounding cadence.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8/r5.anchor: فإن فاصلة آية إبراهيم وهو قوله: (كفار) منسجمة مع فواصل الآيات قبلها وبعدها

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8/r7.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8/r7.claim: Cadence does not act alone: the wording and order also answer the meaning in each context, so one passage is not forced at the expense of another.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8/r7.anchor: فلم يَجُرْ موطن على آخر وهذا غاية الإعجاز ونهاية الحسن في الكلام

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8/r8.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8/r8.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8/r8.claim: Some interpreters offer strained explanations that could be adjusted to fit a different wording; others uncover the arrangement's fine points without obscurity or contrivance.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8/r8.anchor: قسم آخر تمكن من أن يضع يده على أنفس الجواهر في التأليف وأن يستكنه أدق أسرار التعبير من غير تكلف ولا غموض

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8/r12.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8/r12.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8/r12.claim: Ibrahim's context describes human wrongdoing, so its ending names a human trait; al-Nahl's surrounding blessings, including 16:5–15, describe God's attributes, suiting its ending رحيم.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r8/r12.anchor: ذلك أن الآية في سورة إبراهيم في سياق وصف الإنسان وذكر صفاته فختم الآية بصفة الإنسان

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p856/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p856/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p856/r1.claim: He defers the scientific-miracle question to specialists, then suggests mountain formation varies: ألقى may describe volcanic eruptions, earthquakes, or masses brought by celestial bodies, while جعلنا points to another mode of formation.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p856/r1.anchor: أحياناً (ألقينا) وأحياناً يقول (جعلنا) في الكلام عن الجبال بمعنى أن التكوين ليس واحداً

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p354#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p354#3/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p354#3/r1.claim: Qatāda glosses the paths as roads.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p354#3/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ وسبلا لعلكم تهتدون ﴾ قال طرقا

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p354#3/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p354#3/r2.speaker: الحسن
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p354#3/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan glosses the firm mountains as mountains.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p354#3/r2.anchor: عن قتادة عن الحسن في قوله ﴿ وألقى في الأرض رواسي ﴾ قال الجبال

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p354#3/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p354#3/r3.speaker: الحسن
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p354#3/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan reports that the earth nearly swayed when created; by morning mountains had been made, and the angels did not know what they were made from.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p354#3/r3.anchor: سمعت الحسن يقول لما خلقت الأرض كادت أن تميد فقالوا ما هذه بمقرة على ظهرها أحدا فأصبحوا وقد خلقت الجبال

ALUSI-FULL:v14p114#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p114#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p114#2/r1.claim: Rawāsi means firmly fixed mountains; the fuller discussion appeared earlier.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p114#2/r1.anchor: أي جبالا ثوابت وقد مر تمام الكلام في ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v14p114#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p114#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p114#2/r2.claim: The phrase means ‘lest’ or ‘for fear that’ the earth should shake with you; mayd is movement of a great thing.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p114#2/r2.anchor: أي كراهة أن تميد أو لئلا تميد والميد اضطراب الشيء العظيم

ALUSI-FULL:v14p114#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p114#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p114#2/r3.claim: One explanation compares earth to a boat: without heavy masses it would rock, while mountains steady it like weights.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p114#2/r3.anchor: بأنها كسفينة على وجه الماء والسفينة إذا لم يكن فيها أجرام ثقيلة تضطرب وتميل

ALUSI-FULL:v14p114#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p114#2/r4.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v14p114#2/r4.claim: The Imam objects that philosophers’ natural-motion theory would make earth sink in water rather than float and be anchored; a wooden boat differs because air between its parts lets it rock.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p114#2/r4.anchor: على مذهب الحكماء القائلين بأن حركة الأجسام أو سكونها لطبائعها أن الأرض أثقل من الماء

ALUSI-FULL:v14p114#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p114#2/r5.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v14p114#2/r5.claim: On theologians’ view that bodies have no inherent tendencies, mountain weights cannot explain stability, since God alone causes every motion and rest.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p114#2/r5.anchor: على مذهب أهل الحق القائلين بأنه ليس للأجسام طبائع تقتضي السكون أو الحركة

ALUSI-FULL:v14p114#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p114#2/r6.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v14p114#2/r6.claim: The Imam asks why, if water rests by its nature or by God’s power, earth’s stability could not be explained the same way without mountains.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p114#2/r6.anchor: إن سبب سكونه في حيزه المخصوص طبيعته المخصوصة فلم لا يقال في سكون الأرض

ALUSI-FULL:v14p114#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p114#2/r7.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v14p114#2/r7.claim: The earth could move as a whole without inhabitants sensing it, as riders may not sense a boat’s movement; local tremors do not prove otherwise.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p114#2/r7.anchor: أنه يجوز أن تميد الأرض بكليتها ولا تظهر حركتها ولا يشعر بها أهلها

ALUSI-FULL:v14p114#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p114#2/r8.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v14p114#2/r8.claim: The Imam’s solution treats earth as a sphere whose mountain roughness directs heavy masses toward the center like stakes and prevents circular motion.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p114#2/r8.anchor: ثبت بالدلائل اليقينية أن الأرض كرة وثبت أن هذه الجبال على سطح الكرة جارية مجرى خشونات تحصل على وجه هذه الكرة

ALUSI-FULL:v14p114#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p114#2/r9.speaker: البيضاوي
ALUSI-FULL:v14p114#2/r9.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī follows the Imam’s proposed solution.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p114#2/r9.anchor: وقد تابع الإمام في هذا الحل العلامة البيضاوي

ALUSI-FULL:v14p114#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p114#2/r10.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v14p114#2/r10.claim: A critic says the solution fails for both theologians and philosophers.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p114#2/r10.anchor: واعترض عليه بأنه لا وجه لما ذكره على مذهب أهل الحق ولا على مذهب الفلاسفة

ALUSI-FULL:v14p115/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p115/r1.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v14p115/r1.claim: The philosopher critique says earth has a straight natural inclination, not a principle of circular motion, so the Imam’s solution fails on that view.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p115/r1.anchor: إن حق الأرض أن تتحرك بالإستدارة لأن في الأرض ميلا مستقيما وما هو كذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v14p115/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p115/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v14p115/r2.claim: A further objection compares the tallest mountain’s height with earth’s diameter to a tiny fraction of a grain against a large sphere, too small to impede rotation.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p115/r2.anchor: وأورد أيضا على منع الجبال لها من الحركة أنه قد ثبت في الهندسة أن أعظم جبل في الأرض

ALUSI-FULL:v14p115/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p115/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v14p115/r3.claim: Another answer is that God created earth moving for a wisdom known only to Him, then established it with mountains through His customary use of causes.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p115/r3.anchor: ثم قيل : الصحيح أن يقال خلق الله تعالى الأرض مضطربة لحكمة لا يعلمها إلا هو ثم أرساها بالجبال

ALUSI-FULL:v14p115/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p115/r4.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v14p115/r4.claim: A careful scholar says an abstract sphere would either have circular inclination and move, or straight inclination and rest naturally but roll under the slightest push; citing both broadens the argument.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p115/r4.anchor: إن المقصود أن الأرض من حيث كونها كرة حقيقية بسيطة مع قطع النظر عن كونها عنصرا كان حقها أحد الأمرين

ALUSI-FULL:v14p115/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p115/r5.speaker: المجيب
ALUSI-FULL:v14p115/r5.claim: The response says many mountains together may impede motion despite each being small; their effect depends on weight, and hard rock may outweigh porous earth.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p115/r5.anchor: لكن يجوز أن يكون مجموعها مانعا عن حركتها كالحبل المؤلف من الشعرات المخالف حكمه حكم شعرة

ALUSI-FULL:v14p115/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p115/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p115/r6.claim: Al-Ālūsī notes that thirty mountains per region conflicts with the better-known regional counts, totaling 187; he says the response’s objection falls once its intent is understood.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p115/r6.anchor: وهو أن في الإقليم الأول عشرين وفي الثاني سبعة وعشرين وفي الثالث ثلاثة وثلاثين وفي الرابع خمسة وخمسين وفي الخامس ثلاثين

ALUSI-FULL:v14p115/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p115/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v14p115/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya takes alqā as ‘created’ or ‘made’; Al-Ālūsī prefers the more specific sense of bringing mountains into existence by God’s power rather than placing them from earth.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p115/r7.anchor: على ما نقل ابن عطية على التأويل خلق وجعل واختار هو أنه أخص من ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v14p115/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p115/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p115/r8.claim: Unlike ‘I cast affection upon you,’ omitting ʿalā stresses the mountains’ completeness, rootedness, and firmness, like nails in wood.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p115/r8.anchor: ولم يعد بعلي كما في قوله تعالى : ( وألقيت عليك محبة مني ) للإشارة إلى كمال الجبال

ALUSI-FULL:v14p115/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p115/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p115/r9.claim: Al-Ālūsī favors that sitting on a mountain breaks an oath not to sit on earth, since common usage counts mountains as earth, although the verse’s apparent wording may not.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p115/r9.anchor: والظاهر الأول لعد العرف إياها منها وإن كان ظاهر هذه الآية كغيرها عدم العد

ALUSI-FULL:v14p115/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p115/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p115/r10.claim: Wa-anharan coordinates with rawāsi under alqā, whose sense of making or creating governs it without ellipsis, as several grammarians hold.

ALUSI-FULL:v14p115/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p115/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p115/r11.claim: Another parse makes rivers the object of an omitted verb such as ‘made’ or ‘created’; this is not a consensus, despite the attribution to Ibn ʿAṭiyya.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p115/r11.anchor: وجوز أن يكون مفعولا به لفعل مضمر وليس إجماعا خلافا لابن عطية

ALUSI-FULL:v14p116/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116/r1.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116/r1.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ supplies ‘carved’ as the verb, making the coordination one of clauses; the cited line about feeding straw and cold water illustrates the construction.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116/r1.anchor: وقدر أبو البقاء شق والعطف حينئذ من عطف الجمل وكأنه لما كان أغلب منابع الأنهار

ALUSI-FULL:v14p116/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116/r2.claim: Rivers follow mountains because most river sources are in the mountains.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116/r2.anchor: وكأنه لما كان أغلب منابع الأنهار من الجبال ذكر الأنهار بعد ما ذكر الجبال

ALUSI-FULL:v14p116/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116/r3.claim: Subulan means routes leading to people’s destinations.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116/r3.anchor: أي وجعل طرقا لمقاصدكم ( لعلكم تهتدون

ALUSI-FULL:v14p116/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116/r4.claim: The purpose clause most naturally applies to the routes; it may instead explain all preceding signs, which guide people to their maker.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116/r4.anchor: فالتعليل بالنظر إلى قوله تعالى : ( وسبلا ) كما هو الظاهر ويجوز أن يكون تعليلا بالنظر

ALUSI-FULL:v14p116/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116/r5.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116/r5.claim: On the broader reading, tah’tadūn carries a double sense: finding one’s way and being guided to the existence of a wise creator.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p116/r5.anchor: وقيل : تدل على وجود فاعل حكيم ففي قوله تعالى : ( تهتدون ) تورية حينئذ

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p383#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p383#2/r8.speaker: المتأولون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p383#2/r8.claim: Commentators explain ألقى as created and placed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p383#2/r8.anchor: قال المتأولون ألقى بمعنى خلق وجعل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p383#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p383#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p383#2/r9.claim: Ibn Atiyya finds ألقى more specific: God brought the mountains into being by His power and invention, rather than making them from the earth.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p383#2/r9.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وهي عندي أخص من خلق وجعل، وذلك أن ألقى تقتضي أن الله أحدث الجبال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p383#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p383#2/r10.speaker: قيس بن عباد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p383#2/r10.claim: A creation account says the earth first moved; angels feared it could not support anyone, then by morning its stabilizing mountains were there.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p383#2/r10.anchor: ما روي في القصص عن الحسن عن قيس بن عباد، أن الله تعالى لما خلق الأرض، وجعلت تمور

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p383#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p383#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p383#2/r11.claim: رواسي means firmly fixed things, from رسا, to become settled; a poet uses the verb of a peg set in place.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p383#2/r11.anchor: الثوابت، رسا الشيء يرسو إذا ثبت، ومنه قول الشاعر في صفة الوتد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p383#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p383#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p383#2/r12.claim: The clause أن تميد بكم expresses the cause for the mountains' placement.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p383#2/r12.anchor: وأن مفعول من أجله، و «الميد» الاضطراب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p383#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p383#2/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p383#2/r13.anchor: وأن مفعول من أجله، و «الميد» الاضطراب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p383#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p383#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p383#2/r14.claim: أنهارا is accusative under an omitted verb, understood as جعل or خلق.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p383#2/r14.anchor: وقوله أنهارا منصوب بفعل مضمر تقديره وجعل أو وخلق أنهارا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p383#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p383#2/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p383#2/r15.claim: The shared need to supply a verb for أنهارا supports his view that ألقى is more specific than simply خلق.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p383#2/r15.anchor: وإجماعهم على إضمار هذا الفعل دليل على خصوص ل ألقى ولو كانت ألقى بمعنى خلق لم يحتج

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p383#2/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p383#2/r17.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p383#2/r17.claim: One possible sense is that people find their way while traveling along the roads.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p383#2/r17.anchor: وقوله لعلكم تهتدون في مشيكم وتصرفكم في السبل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p383#2/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p383#2/r18.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p383#2/r18.claim: He prefers that people be guided to the Creator by reflecting on these created things, which God made as signs.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p383#2/r18.anchor: وهذا التأويل هو البارع، أي سخر وألقى وجعل أنهارا وسبلا لعل البشر يعتبر ويرشد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p435/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p435/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p435/r1.claim: Rawāsi are mountains fixed firmly in the earth.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p435/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى ( وألقى في الأرض رواسي ) أي نصب فيها جبالا ثوابت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p435/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p435/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p435/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains an tamīda as “lest it sway,” or “for fear that it sway.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p435/r2.anchor: ( أن تميد ) أي لئلا تميد وقال الزجاج كراهة أن تميد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p435/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p435/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p435/r3.claim: The idiom māda al-rajul yamīdu refers to a man becoming dizzy, as if turned around.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p435/r3.anchor: يقال ماد الرجل يميد ميدا إذا أدير به

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p435/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p435/r4.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p435/r4.claim: Ibn Qutayba defines mayd as movement and inclination; a person may sway while walking.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p435/r4.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة الميد الحركة والميل يقال فلان يميد في مشيته أي يتكفأ

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p435/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p435/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p435/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj supplies “He made paths in it”: alqā here carries the sense of jaʿala, “made.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p435/r5.anchor: قال الزجاج المعنى وجعل فيها سبلا لأن معنى ألقى جعل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p435/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p435/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p435/r7.claim: The paths allow people to find their destinations.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p435/r7.anchor: ( ولعلكم تهتدون ) أي لكي تهتدوا إلى مقاصدكم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p563#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p563#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p563#2/r1.claim: God made rivers flow from one place to another as provision: they cross regions, deserts and mountains to reach inhabited lands, in many sizes and speeds, sometimes seasonally and sometimes continuously, as God wills and measures.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p563#2/r1.anchor: وقوله: {وأنهارا وسبلا} أي: وجعل فيها أنهارا تجري من مكان إلى مكان آخر، رزقا للعباد،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p563#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p563#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p563#2/r2.claim: God made roads connecting lands and even cut passages through mountains for people to travel.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p563#2/r2.anchor: وكذلك جعل فيها سبلا أي: طرقا يسلك فيها من بلاد إلى بلاد، حتى إنه تعالى ليقطع الجبل

MUJAHID:v1p346#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p346#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p346#2/r1.claim: Mujahid glosses the earth's swaying as its tipping or overturning with you.
MUJAHID:v1p346#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ أن تميد بكم ﴾ يقول أن تكفأ بكم

NASAFI-FULL:v2p252/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p252/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p252/r2.claim: The phrase means lest the earth sway or shake; one analysis supplies a deleted noun meaning aversion, another supplies “lest,” and deletion of a noun is common.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p252/r2.anchor: كراهية أن تميل بكم أو تضطرب أو لئلا تميد بكم لكن حذف المضاف أكثر

NASAFI-FULL:v2p252/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p252/r3.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v2p252/r3.claim: An account says the new earth swayed and angels feared it could support no one; mountains fixed it, though angels did not know what it was created from.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p252/r3.anchor: قيل خلق الله الأرض فجعلت تميد فقالت الملائكة ما هي بمقر أحد على ظهرها فأصبحت وقد أرسيت بالجبال لم تدر الملائكة مم خلقت

NASAFI-FULL:v2p252/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p252/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p252/r4.claim: The implied verb for rivers is “made,” because alqā here carries the sense of jaʿala.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p252/r4.anchor: وجعل فيها انهارا لأن القي فيه معنى جعل

NASAFI-FULL:v2p252/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p252/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p252/r5.anchor: ﴿ وسبلا ﴾ طرقا ﴿ لعلكم تهتدون ﴾ إلى مقاصدكم

NASAFI-FULL:v2p252/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p252/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p252/r6.claim: The roads lead to destinations or recognition of God's oneness.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p252/r6.anchor: إلى مقاصدكم أو إلى توحيد ربكم

QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r1.claim: Rawāsi are fixed mountains; rasā means becoming firm and remaining, as the cited poem uses ترسو for steadiness.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r1.anchor: أي جبالا ثابتة. رسا يرسو إذا ثبت وأقام.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r2.claim: The poetic line uses ترسو for remaining firm when the coward's soul rises; its poet is not named.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r2.anchor: فصبرت عارفة لذلك حرة ترسو إذا نفس الجبان تطلع

QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r3.speaker: الكوفيون
QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r3.claim: Kufan grammarians take أن تميد as purpose: so the earth does not sway with you.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r4.speaker: البصريون
QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r4.claim: Basran grammarians take the phrase as expressing aversion to the earth swaying.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r4.anchor: وكراهية أن تميد على قول البصريين

QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r5.claim: Mayd is movement and rocking side to side; branches sway and a man may use the verb for strutting.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r5.anchor: والميد: الاضطراب يمينا وشمالا ماد الشيء يميد ميدا إذا تحرك

QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r6.speaker: وهب بن منبه
QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r6.claim: Wahb says the new earth swayed; angels feared none could live on it, then found it anchored by mountains without knowing their origin.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r6.anchor: قال وهب بن منبه: خلق الله الأرض فجعلت تميد وتمور، فقالت الملائكة

QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r7.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r7.claim: Ali reports that the earth shook and objected to bearing sinners and corpses, so God anchored it with seen and unseen mountains.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r7.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه: لما خلق الله الأرض قمصت ومالت

QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r8.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r8.claim: Anas reports the Prophet saying mountains steadied the earth; angels asked what was stronger, culminating in a person's secret charity.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r8.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r9.speaker: أبو عيسى
QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r9.claim: Al-Tirmidhī calls the Prophetic report gharīb and says it is known as marfūʿ only through this route.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r9.anchor: قال أبو عيسى: هذا حديث غريب لا نعرفه مرفوعا إلا من هذا الوجه

QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r10.claim: The verse strongly establishes using causes: God could have stilled the earth without mountains but chose this means.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r10.anchor: قلت: وفي هذه الآية أدل دليل على استعمال الأسباب، وقد كان قادرا على سكونها دون الجبال

QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r11.claim: The omitted verb for rivers may mean He made them in the earth or cast them into it.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r11.anchor: أي وجعل فيها أنهارا، أو ألقى فيها أنهارا.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r13.claim: The routes help people reach their intended destinations without losing their way or becoming confused.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:15/r13.anchor: أي إلى حيث تقصدون من البلاد فلا تضلون ولا تتحيرون

BURSEVI:v5p15#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p15#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p15#2/r1.claim: The earth is spherical and lies at the world's center; its name is linked to the verb for consuming, since it consumes human bodies.
BURSEVI:v5p15#2/r1.anchor: هي كروية الشكل محلها وسط العالم وسميت بالأرض لأنها تأرض

BURSEVI:v5p15#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p15#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p15#2/r2.claim: God set firm mountains in the earth without support, picturing them as pebbles cast by a hand to portray divine greatness and power over every difficult thing.
BURSEVI:v5p15#2/r2.anchor: جبالا ثوابت من غير سبب ولا ظهير كأنها حصيات قبضهن قابض بيده فنبذهن في الأرض

BURSEVI:v5p15#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p15#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p15#2/r3.claim: Rawāsi means firmly settled mountains; it is the plural of rāsiyah, with a feminine ending because it describes mountains.
BURSEVI:v5p15#2/r3.anchor: من رسا الشيء إذا نبت جمع راسية والتاء للتأنيث على أنها صفة جبال

BURSEVI:v5p15#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p15#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p15#2/r4.claim: The phrase is an object of purpose; mayd means movement or swaying, and the earth's being anchored is to prevent it from shaking people.
BURSEVI:v5p15#2/r4.anchor: الميد الحركة والميل يقال ما ديميد ميدا تحرك

BURSEVI:v5p15#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p15#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p15#2/r5.claim: The earth was created unstable on water, then God anchored it with mountains according to His customary ordering of things through causes; Bursevī gives their number as 6,673, excluding hills.
BURSEVI:v5p15#2/r5.anchor: وقد خلق الله الأرض مضطربة لكونها على الماء ثم أرساها بالجبال وهي ستة آلاف وستمائة وثلاثة وسبعون

BURSEVI:v5p15#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p15#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p15#2/r6.claim: Mountains support the earth as bones support an animal's body; he compares this with the soothsayer Satih, whose body lacked bones except the tailbone and could not hold itself upright.
BURSEVI:v5p15#2/r6.anchor: فالأرض بلا جبال كاللحم بلا عظام فكما أن وجود الحيوان وجسده إنما يستمسك بالعظم

BURSEVI:v5p15#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p15#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p15#2/r7.claim: Anhar is the plural of nahr, also pronounced nahar, and means a watercourse; the word “cast” also carries the sense of making, so rivers were made in the earth.

BURSEVI:v5p15#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p15#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p15#2/r8.claim: He illustrates the rivers with the Euphrates at Kufa, Tigris at Baghdad, Jayhun at Balkh, Jeyhan at Adana, Sihon in India, Saihan at al-Massisa, and the Nile in Egypt.
BURSEVI:v5p15#2/r8.anchor: مثل الفرات نهر الكوفة ودجلة نهر بغداد وجيحون نهر بلخ وجيحان نهر اذنه

BURSEVI:v5p15#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p15#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p15#2/r9.claim: Subul is the plural of sabil, meaning roads or clear ways.
BURSEVI:v5p15#2/r9.anchor: وطرقا مختلفة جمع سبيل وهو الطريق وما وضح

BURSEVI:v5p15#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p15#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p15#2/r10.claim: The purpose of making roads is that people may find their destinations and dwellings.
BURSEVI:v5p15#2/r10.anchor: إرادة أن تهتدوا بها إلى مقاصدكم ومنازلكم
